question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-8 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. What are the dimensions of the eigenspaces ${V}_{-6}$ and ${V}_{2}$ corresponding to eigenvalues $\lambda =-6$ and $\lambda =2$ of $A$, respectively?
question.worked_solution:
First, we write down the characteristic equation $\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-8-\lambda  & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2-\lambda  & 0 \\ -5 & -1 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ (2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-8-\lambda  & 4 \\ -5 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ (2-\lambda )((-8-\lambda )(4-\lambda )+20)=0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda -12)=0 \\ (2-\lambda )(\lambda +6)(\lambda -2)=0 \\ (\lambda -2)^{2}(\lambda +6)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=2$ (double root) and ${\lambda }_{3}=-6$ (simple root).

Let's now consider the eigenspaces corresponding to each eigenvector:

- First, we consider $\lambda =-6.$ Since ${V}_{-6}$ corresponds to a simple root, we obtain 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-6})=1.
$$

- Then, we consider $\lambda =2,$ which is a repeated root of the characteristic equation. To find the dimension of ${V}_{2},$ we row-reduce the matrix $(A-2I)\text{x}=0:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-10 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{2})=2.
$$
